questions.q: Why does the lesson recommend pinning your three capstone projects instead of as many repos as possible?
options: A reviewer forms an opinion quickly skimming pinned repos, and a few complete, documented projects beat many abandoned ones
GitHub only allows a single pinned repository per account
Pinning more than one repo is technically impossible
Tutorial clones are the strongest signal of ability a repo can give
questions.explain: The lesson states three complete, well-documented projects beat fifteen abandoned ones, since a reviewer judges a profile quickly.

questions.q: Which section does the lesson say most directly influences a hiring decision, and why?
options: Key design decisions, because a reviewer can run the tests themselves but can't read your reasoning anywhere else
The software license section, because legal compliance is the top hiring factor
The getting-started install steps, since no other part of a README matters as much
The contributors list, since team size is the main signal reviewers look for
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly calls out the design-decisions section as the one that most influences hiring, since reasoning isn't otherwise visible.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what makes a verified contract link on a block explorer especially valuable in a portfolio?
options: It's the one piece of evidence a reviewer can check without having to trust the candidate's word at all
It automatically increases the contract's gas efficiency
It replaces the need for any tests to exist
It hides the contract's source code from competitors
questions.explain: The lesson frames contract verification as uniquely valuable because it's publicly checkable, unlike a resume claim.

questions.q: Why does the lesson recommend including a short demo video in a project's README?
options: Because most reviewers won't clone the repo and run it themselves, so a recording gets most of the benefit of a live demo
Because demo videos are required by GitHub's terms of service
Because a demo video replaces the need for a verified contract link
Because written documentation is never read by technical reviewers
questions.explain: The lesson explains that a short screen recording substitutes for the live walkthrough most reviewers won't have time to run themselves.

questions.q: What does the lesson identify as a common mistake that undermines an otherwise strong GitHub profile?
options: Pinning a repo that is clearly an unmodified tutorial clone with no README of your own
Including too many tests in a project
Writing a README that is too short to read in one sitting
Linking a verified contract directly from the README
questions.explain: The lesson lists pinning unmodified tutorial clones as a mistake that signals the opposite of real engineering depth.
